result.choiceRationale: G-AF3 is the highest expected research value per budget unit: it is the only candidate that directly generates new evidence (variation across encounter variants) rather than closing out or packaging already-established mechanisms. It is closable within one budget unit (create 2-3 variants, re-run probes, separate surviving priors from overfit). R-P5 is near-complete but its remaining work is mechanical acceptance/commit/release — low marginal research value and low ambiguity. HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit with only conditional build work ("only if measurable"), so it may not consume the budget productively. H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery — defer until unblocked. F-C2-BLOCKED is a negative control with a dominant external admission blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) that no research budget can resolve — defer.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether G-AF3's perturbation probes reveal that AF002 priors survive topology/position/resource/target variation, or instead collapse into fixed-encounter overfit — this discriminates prior-generalization vs defect-discovery.
result.selectionFalsifier: If G-AF3's encounter variants cannot be made materially different within the budget (e.g., Genesis/Scenario constraints prevent real variation), then the candidate is not closable and HOST-PKG (which has a concrete audit path) would be the better allocation.
